properties.decision:
RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Alex (`who:alex`), relayed by Anthony 2026-08-14.

HIS WORDS: *"I don't think it should be focused on a specific topic like software engineering as I'd like to use it for other projects like my shop."*

🛑 THE INTENT IS ALREADY ACCEPTED, SO THIS IS NOT A NEW REQUIREMENT. `req:design-anything` (ACCEPTED): *"Software, hardware, a document, a process — the vocabulary stays neutral."* What Alex hit is not the vocabulary — it is EVERYTHING WRAPPED AROUND IT. The served instructions and skills assume a codebase throughout: Artifacts are source files with checksums, `link-artifacts` opens on *"Unity C#, a spec, a doc"*, `ci-gate` is a build gate, the loop's step 3 is *"build only what the graph specifies"*, and his own example — how database migrations are performed — is the one part of his note that IS software. **The nouns are neutral and the worked examples, defaults and skills are not.**

⭐ SO THE HONEST STATEMENT OF THE GAP: reflow2 can MODEL a shop today, and nothing in what a shop owner would actually read shows them how. That is a delivery problem, and it is the same shape as two findings already on the record — `req:a-discipline-is-delivered-at-the-tool-not-in-a-catalogue`, and the installer wording Alex himself caught, where the information existed somewhere the person was not.

✅ TWO MEASURED FACTS THE OPTIONS HAVE TO LIVE WITH:
  · `Project.domain` IS WRITTEN AND NEVER READ (`req:framework-is-chosen-not-defaulted`). The field that would carry "this is a shop, not a service" already exists and drives nothing.
  · The Environment / EnvironmentRule compliance layer was DESIGNED IN FULL AND NEVER BUILT, and `dec:idea-the-environment-compliance-layer-was-designed-and-never-built` says in as many words that it *"is what makes 'design a house' concrete"*. The non-software story has a designed, unbuilt half already sitting in the graph.

OPTIONS, NONE CHOSEN.
(a) NOTHING TO DO — the requirement is accepted and the vocabulary is neutral; a competent agent adapts. Counter: the second user, holding the tool, concluded the opposite from what he actually saw.
(b) ONE WORKED NON-SOFTWARE EXAMPLE end to end — his shop is the obvious candidate and he is volunteering to be the test case. Cheapest thing that would have prevented his impression, and it produces evidence rather than assertion.
(c) MAKE `Project.domain` READ — let it select examples and defaults. **This is the option the design's own rules already point at:** `req:a-vocabulary-distinction-proves-it-is-read` says a distinction no computation reads should be removed or made real, and `domain` is currently the former.
(d) BUILD THE ENVIRONMENT COMPLIANCE LAYER, on the grounds that regulation and physical context are what non-software design mostly IS. Largest, and it has its own open decision already.
(e) SAY IT PLAINLY IN THE DOCS — reflow2 is software-first today, other domains work but are untravelled. Costs nothing, makes no promise it cannot keep, and is the only option that stays honest whichever of the others is chosen.

📌 WORTH KNOWING WHO IS ASKING: this is the third distinct thread where Alex's use diverges from Anthony's, and his projects are the only non-reflow2, non-flo2 evidence the design has. `dec:idea-feedback-collection-is-asked-once-and-recorded` — which ALEX HIMSELF ASKED FOR — is the mechanism that would stop each of these arriving as a relayed email.
properties.name: OPEN — `req:design-anything` is accepted and the DELIVERY is still software-shaped; what closes the gap between a neutral vocabulary and a toolchain full of code?
properties.rationale: Captured under the brainstorm skill. Recorded as an open question rather than as a requirement precisely BECAUSE the requirement already exists and is accepted: the useful question is not "should reflow2 design anything" (settled, yes) but "what is still software-shaped after that was settled", and framing it the first way would have produced a duplicate of `req:design-anything` and lost Alex's actual point.
